title: The terminal is a window for entering commands
body: A terminal is a window through which you send text-based commands to a computer. PowerShell, CMD, and Bash differ in appearance and some of their commands, but they all execute commands and operate based on the current folder.
detail: Beginners should first check which folder they are running commands from. Even the same command can target different files depending on the location. Checking the path displayed in the command prompt, the `cd` or `Set-Location` commands, and the file path can help reduce many execution errors. Checking your current location before running a command is essential.

title: Current folder and path
body: The current folder is the base directory from which the command is executed. An error indicating that a file cannot be found may occur not because the file actually does not exist, but because the current folder is different. Therefore, check the path before executing the command.
detail: In PowerShell, you use `Set-Location` to change directories. Relative paths are interpreted relative to the current directory, while absolute paths specify the full location starting from the drive or root. If you cannot find a validation script or JSON file, you should first verify that the current directory is the project root. It is especially important to check the location before running the script.

title: What are Ubuntu and WSL?
body: Ubuntu is a Linux distribution, and WSL is a feature that allows you to run a Linux environment within Windows. Although it is distinct from Python itself, you’ll often come across it when reading documentation on server and AI development.
detail: Learning Python itself is different from learning Ubuntu. However, since documentation for servers, AI tools, CUDA, and deployment is often written with Linux in mind, familiarity with Ubuntu or WSL makes it easier to read development documentation. On Windows, PowerShell is frequently used, while on Ubuntu or WSL, Bash and the `apt` command are commonly used.

title: sudo runs with administrator privileges
body: In Linux, `sudo` means to run a command with administrative privileges. While it may be necessary for tasks that affect the entire system, it is not a one-size-fits-all solution that should be used with every command.
detail: Tasks that affect the entire computer, such as installing packages or configuring the system, may require `sudo`. Conversely, if you force a solution to a Python package issue in a project folder using `sudo`, it can cause file ownership or permissions to become corrupted. When an error occurs, you should first check whether the task requires elevated privileges.

title: apt and pip are used for different types of installations.
body: apt installs Ubuntu system packages, while pip installs Python packages. Although both look like installation commands, they differ in what they install and their scope. In a virtual environment, check the pip installation as well.
detail: System tools such as `git` and `build-essential` are often installed using `apt`. Python libraries such as `requests`, `numpy`, and `pandas` are installed using `pip`. In projects that use virtual environments, Python packages are typically installed using the command `python -m pip` to ensure they are compatible with the current environment.

title: A virtual environment is a project-specific Python environment
body: A virtual environment separates package installation locations and reduces project version conflicts. Activation is a PATH convenience, not a requirement; the environment interpreter can be called directly. Record dependency versions and supported Python, then run tests to reproduce the setup more closely.

title: requirements.txt is a list of dependencies
body: requirements.txt lists package requirements for pip; it is not automatically a complete environment lock. Consider pinning, Python and OS constraints, and transitive dependencies. Verify the installation by running the program or tests.

title: Basic Git Workflow: Check → Commit → Push → Upload
body: Git is a tool for tracking changes to code. Typically, you use `status` to check the current status, `add` to stage changes, `commit` to record them, and `push` to upload them to a remote repository like GitHub.
detail: `git add` is not yet a final commit; it is the step where you select the files to include in this commit. `git commit` creates a local commit, and `git push` sends it to the remote repository. For beginners, it’s important to get into the habit of frequently checking `status` to see which files have been modified and what to commit.

title: "clone" and "pull" retrieve code
body: clone creates a new local repository from a remote. pull fetches remote changes and integrates them into the current branch, so it is not simply overwriting files with 'the latest version' and may conflict. Check the current branch and uncommitted work first.

title: CUDA is a gateway to NVIDIA GPUs
body: nvidia-smi reports GPU and driver state, while torch.cuda.is_available() tests whether the selected PyTorch environment can use CUDA. A system CUDA toolkit is not always required because a PyTorch build may include runtime components. Also inspect tensor/model devices and VRAM.
